Vertical mirror-stack of a 3×3 grid (`size=3` always): output rows = `[r0,r1,r2, r2,r1,r0]`, rest of the 30×30 canvas is background padding. **See `task172.md` for the full rule, floor proof, sub-30 sweep, and don't-do log — it all ports verbatim.** (NOTE: this file is gitignored and has been seen to revert under the concurrent loop; the durable record lives in the git-tracked `task172.md`.)

## Algorithm sketch

`out[r] = in[idx[r]]` on axis=2, `idx = [0,1,2, 2,1,0, 3×24]`. One node:

```
Gather(input[1,10,30,30] F32, idx INT64[30], axis=2) → output[1,10,30,30]
```

Dominant charged tensor: `idx` INT64 `[30]` = 30 params. There are no charged intermediates because the only node output is the graph `output`.

Exact floor reason: the output must be the full `[1,10,30,30]` one-hot canvas, and the required row sequence is not an affine/transpose-only view. A zero-memory solution must be one op whose result is `output`; for this rule that means a `Gather` over axis 2. That `Gather` requires one index per output row, so params are at least 30. Dtype shrink cannot reduce params, and sub-INT32 index dtypes are rejected. Every shorter-basis construction needs at least one counted row-block intermediate, so it jumps above 30.

## Crop-to-active-grid analysis (2026-05-19, worker-7)

**Result: NOT VIABLE — Gather output is the model output; crop adds memory.**

This task has a single `Gather(input [1,10,30,30], idx[30], axis=2-or-3)` node. The Gather output IS the model's final output tensor; ORT does not count it in internal memory tracking (memory=0). The advisory's "30×30 intermediate" is this output tensor.

Any prepended `Slice(input→[1,10,N,30])` would create a new counted intermediate (e.g. [1,10,4,30]=4800 bytes for task116), catastrophically increasing cost from 30→4830+.

Additionally, output rows 6–29 map to a background input row (idx values ≥ N after the active region); padding with zeros would produce incorrect (non-background) output values.

**Do NOT attempt crop for this task in future sessions.**
